questions.problem:
A rectangular plate occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2\}$
with mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=x{e}^{2y}\,\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

Using the formula for ${I}_{y},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\int }_{2}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot x{e}^{2y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}[{\int }_{2}^{4}{x}^{3}{e}^{2y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{e}^{2y}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{2}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}60{e}^{2y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[30{e}^{2y}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =120-30 \\  & =90.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $y$-axis is $90\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.$

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the lines $y=0$, $x=4$, and the curve $y=\sqrt{x}$, as shown above. If the mass density function of $D$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=3y,$ find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{x}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14153799/assets/dd5ee021dd73317a775c0ea653212f7ee5545f8c6854e6a9daabdc93b5c3b9c0.png)

Using the formula for ${I}_{0},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot 3y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}3{x}^{2}y+3{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{3}{4}{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3}{8}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =96+16 \\  & =112.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14153799/assets/de3753a45554be28283e74116510ff6c3b67560fce79d1570c819a215f6e10f3.png)

A triangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the $x$-axis and the lines $y=3x$ and $y=4-x,$ as shown above. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,\frac{y}{3}\le x\le 4-y\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14153799/assets/47c897bd58a23965d9c36f683553c0817afa8bc2e37ed53a432edcd62b386e55.png)

The area of the triangular plate $D$ is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3=6.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, every unit of area contains the same amount of mass. Therefore, the mass density is constant and is given by the total mass divided by the total area:

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{6}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{y/3}^{4-y}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}[{\int }_{y/3}^{4-y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}(4-y-\frac{1}{3}y)\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{y}^{2}-\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{[\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{3}{y}^{4}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{6}(36-27) \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

A triangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the $y$-axis and the lines $y=\frac{x}{2}$ and $y=3-x,$ as shown above. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,\frac{x}{2}\le y\le 3-x\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14153799/assets/6c2cec5e919c25623396b5ba5f052481623a868c7520aa8e3d1d3eb34f3a4a58.png)

The area of the triangular plate $D$ is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 3=3.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, every unit of area contains the same amount of mass. Therefore, the mass density is constant and is given by the total mass divided by the total area:

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}[{\int }_{x/2}^{3-x}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}(3-x-\frac{x}{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{[{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{8}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(8-6) \\  & =\frac{2M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the plate that occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the polar circles $r=1$ and $r=\sqrt[5]{2}$ and the polar rays $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}$ in the first quadrant, as shown above. The mass density function of the plate is given by $\lambda (x,y)=15y.$ Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (r,\theta ),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin, in polar coordinates, is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, note that the region $D$ in polar coordinates can be expressed as

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le \sqrt[5]{2},\,\,\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{3}\}.
$$

Also, the mass density function in polar coordinates is 

$$
\lambda (r,\theta )=15r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[5]{2}}15r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot {r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[5]{2}}15{r}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =({\int }_{1}^{\sqrt[5]{2}}5{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3}3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & ={r}^{5}\,{|}_{1}^{\sqrt[5]{2}}\cdot (-{cos}^{3}⁡\theta )\,{|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /3} \\  & =(2-1)\cdot (-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}-1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
